verdict.root_cause: Checkout failures originate at the ShippingService/GetQuote call. Every sampled failing trace terminates at checkoutservice's client span for that call with ERROR status propagating up through PlaceOrder to the frontend, while cart/Redis, product catalog, feature flag and currency spans all complete cleanly, and no payment, email or broker span is ever reached (tr_c49390dc4046). The shippingservice server span itself completes in ~2ms without an error flag, so the callee answers fast and considers itself fine while the caller treats the response as an error — a fast error return, not a stall. That signature points to a wrong or incompatible shippingservice artifact rather than latency or saturation. checkoutservice is a victim: it stayed up, kept accepting orders, logged no errors, and had no deploy or config change in the window (tr_fc2ccaca02d1, tr_eb8fbdfb53a8). The partial error ratio peaking near 27.8% with dips to zero is consistent with only part of the shipping replica set serving the bad artifact (tr_35b8ab805d0d). Critically, no dispatch ever examined shippingservice's own changes, metrics or logs, so the artifact hypothesis is inferred from trace shape and elimination, not observed.
verdict.reasoning: Trace evidence localizes the terminal error to the checkoutservice->shippingservice boundary with everything upstream healthy (tr_c49390dc4046), and zero server-side error ratios at cartservice and productcatalogservice remove the other checkout dependencies (tr_4e15d7efe181, tr_7161353dc65d). Logs corroborate the truncation point: orders start but never reach payment, email or the message write after ~05:17 (tr_fc2ccaca02d1). Mechanism follows from shape — failing traces finish in 8-15ms with the callee span at ~2ms, so nothing is waiting, excluding dependency_latency; no saturation signal and no crash or telemetry gap, so resource_exhaustion is unsupported (though CPU, memory and pool series were never queried, so it is unrefuted rather than excluded). With no change records on checkoutservice or paymentservice (tr_eb8fbdfb53a8, tr_448f1cc832db), the causing act sits in an unqueried service; a fast rejection by a callee that believes it succeeded fits a mismatched artifact better than a wrong config value, hence bad_deploy and rollback of shippingservice.
open_questions: No dispatch touched shippingservice itself — its change history, error rate, and logs are entirely unobserved, so the wrong-artifact mechanism is inferred, not confirmed; a bad config value or contract mismatch on shippingservice would look identical from the caller.
Change queries covered only 05:06-05:21 despite asking for two hours, so any change landing between 03:16 and 05:06 on any service is unexamined.

No latency, CPU, memory, connection- or thread-pool, or queue-depth series were ever returned for checkoutservice, and checkoutservice logs were truncated across roughly 05:06-05:17, leaving onset behavior and saturation unruled-out rather than excluded.
